name: s16-bound
title: Bound methods carry the instance
spec: Left: code chip bob.give_raise(0.1). Arrow to a bound method box holding two things: the instance bob and the function give_raise. Right: the same call written as Person.give_raise(bob, 0.1), the explicit form, labelled same result (green). Orange note: self is the instance passed as the first argument.
cap: A bound method pairs the function with its instance, so obj.method() passes self automatically.

name: s16-delegation
title: Inheritance versus delegation
spec: Two panels. Left panel Inheritance (is-a): class Manager points up to class Person. Right panel Delegation (like-a): class Wrapper holds an attribute pointing at a wrapped object and forwards calls to it, through __getattr__ (green). Bottom bar: inherit to specialise, delegate to wrap.
cap: Inheritance specialises a class, while delegation wraps another object and forwards calls to it.

name: s16-methodkinds
title: Instance, class and static methods
spec: Three rows: a code chip and a statement of what it receives. Plain method def m(self): receives the instance ; @classmethod def c(cls): receives the class ; @staticmethod def s(): receives nothing extra (green). Orange note: use classmethod for per-class data and alternative constructors.
cap: A method receives the instance, the class or nothing, depending on how it is declared.

name: s16-slots
title: Instance dictionary versus slots
spec: Two panels. Left panel Normal instance: object box with a per-instance __dict__ that can grow new attributes (flexible, larger). Right panel With __slots__ = ('x', 'y'): object box with fixed slots x and y, no __dict__, and assigning another name raises AttributeError (orange), smaller memory (green).
cap: __slots__ replaces the per-instance dictionary with fixed slots, trading flexibility for memory.
